original_question: Given two distinct sets P1 and P2 of odd primes none of which is a subset of the other, is it true that ⟨CTP1(Z), CTP2(Z)⟩ ⪇ CTP1 ∪P2(Z)? See the definition of CTP(Z) in 17.60.
target_in_paper: Problem 21.75 in the section "New Problems (21st issue, 2026)".
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact official problem almost verbatim: it has the right objects (the groups CT_{P_1}(Z), CT_{P_2}(Z), and CT_{P_1\cup P_2}(Z)), the right hypotheses on P_1 and P_2 (distinct sets of odd primes, neither contained in the other), and the right conclusion being asked (whether the subgroup they generate is properly contained in CT_{P_1\cup P_2}(Z)).
missing_details: The draft is not stand-alone because it refers externally to "the definition of CTP(Z) in 17.60" instead of stating that definition.
To define CT_P(Z), one must also define CT(Z), since CT_P(Z) is a subgroup of CT(Z).
To define CT(Z), one must define the residue-class notation r(m)=r+mZ for integers 0<=r<m.

One must define a class transposition τ_{r_1(m_1),r_2(m_2)}: it is only defined for disjoint residue classes r_1(m_1) and r_2(m_2), it swaps r_1+km_1 with r_2+km_2 for every k in Z, and fixes all other integers.

The condition on allowed moduli should be stated explicitly: in CT_P(Z), the generating class transpositions are those whose moduli m_1,m_2 have all prime divisors in P∪{2} (equivalently, all odd prime divisors lie in P).
The bracket notation <CT_{P_1}(Z),CT_{P_2}(Z)> should be unpacked as "the subgroup of CT(Z) generated by CT_{P_1}(Z) and CT_{P_2}(Z)."
The symbol for proper inclusion should be spelled out in words for full stand-alone clarity: the question asks whether the generated subgroup is a proper subgroup of CT_{P_1\cup P_2}(Z).
refined_question: For integers 0 <= r < m, write r(m)=r+mZ. If r_1(m_1) and r_2(m_2) are disjoint residue classes of Z, let τ_{r_1(m_1),r_2(m_2)} be the involution of Z that interchanges r_1+km_1 and r_2+km_2 for every k in Z and fixes all other integers. Let CT(Z) be the subgroup of Sym(Z) generated by all such class transpositions. For a set P of odd primes, let CT_P(Z) <= CT(Z) be the subgroup generated by those class transpositions τ_{r_1(m_1),r_2(m_2)} whose moduli m_1 and m_2 have only prime factors in P∪{2}. If P_1 and P_2 are distinct sets of odd primes with P_1 not contained in P_2 and P_2 not contained in P_1, is the subgroup generated by CT_{P_1}(Z) and CT_{P_2}(Z) necessarily a proper subgroup of CT_{P_1\cup P_2}(Z)?
justification: The draft is aiming at Problem 21.75 exactly, not at the earlier broader isomorphism question in Problem 17.60. Problem 21.75 states the same incomparable-set hypothesis and the same proper-subgroup question. The only reason the draft is not fully stand-alone is that the notation CT_P(Z) depends on the back-reference in 17.60, which itself depends on the definitions of class transpositions and CT(Z) given in 17.57. So the faithful refinement is to keep the statement of 21.75 unchanged in substance while expanding those definitions inline.
